verdicts.reason: The new `describe "expandable_first_post?"` block opens with a blank line and closes with one, and embeddable_host_spec's describe block does the same; that is exactly what Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody flags. The repo ships no .rubocop.yml, so the rule is not actually enforced here, but the stray lines are really there.

_lookupSubType returns undefined when the id is absent from the sideloaded collection (store.js.es6:157-187). The singular branch only assigns and deletes the raw key when hydration succeeded; the plural branch assigns the mapped array and deletes obj[k] unconditionally, so missing records become undefined holes and the original ids are gone.

Ran the literal regex against sample hosts: 'example.software' and 'example.museum' both fail because of `[a-z]{2,5}`. The model has no custom validation message either, so the admin only sees the generic 'is invalid'.
The added block reads `describe 'with an emeddable host' do` — 'embeddable' is misspelled.

The format regex explicitly allows `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` and before_validation only strips the scheme and the path, so 'example.com:3000' saves intact. record_for_host then compares `lower(host)` to `URI(...).host`, which I confirmed in ruby returns 'example.com' with no port — the stored row can never match.

Both new specs contain a single example asserting `Controller < Admin::AdminController`. No create/update/destroy request is exercised, so the nil-record path (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:8-13) and the nil-host NoMethodError are untested.

category_fabricator.rb now holds only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category. Fabrication loads the whole spec/fabricators directory, so nothing breaks — the filenames are simply wrong.

This is the pre-existing :private_category fabricator relocated byte-for-byte from category_fabricator.rb; the diff changes none of it. Every caller (spec/components/guardian_spec.rb:278, spec/models/invite_spec.rb:132, spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb:757, spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1455, spec/controllers/posts_controller_spec.rb:840) passes `group:`, so the described raise does not occur.

ApplicationSerializer declares `embed :ids, include: true` at class level, and EmbeddingSerializer inherits it; the per-association `embed: :ids` does not turn root embedding off. The identical pattern on UserSerializer's featured_user_badges is relied on by the client, which reads the sideloaded root `user_badges` array — so the embeddable_hosts array is sideloaded and hydration works.

`execute(...)[0]['id']` runs before the `if category_id == 0` fallback. PG::Result#[] raises IndexError on an empty result, and the join only matches when a site_settings row named embed_category exists whose value equals a category name — which is false on fresh installs and on every site that left embed_category at its '' default. Sibling migrations guard exactly this (20140715190552_remove_uncategorized_parents.rb:4 checks `uncat && uncat[0] && uncat[0]['value']`; 20130625170842_remove_access_password.rb:4 checks `result[0] and ...`).

_lookupSubType resolves category via Discourse.Category.findById, which returns undefined when the id is not in the client-side category list — and Site#categories omits the uncategorized category when allow_uncategorized_topics is false, which is exactly the id the server assigns by default. edit() then sets categoryId to undefined and save() posts category_id: undefined, which the controller silently rewrites to uncategorized.
The delete action chains only `.then(...)` on destroyRecord, while save() in the same file ends with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. A rejected destroy leaves the row rendered and shows the user nothing.

expandable_first_post? is now `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` — it no longer consults embeddable hosts at all. The retained example 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' lost its setup line and now passes because embed_truncate defaults to false, so it asserts nothing about its stated subject.

The SQL side lowercases the column but the bind value is passed through unchanged. I confirmed in ruby that URI('http://EvilTrout.com/x').host returns 'EvilTrout.com', so a mixed-case referer host fails a comparison that was clearly written to be case-insensitive; it needs `host.downcase`.

d-button binds `translatedTitle` to the title attribute, which is empty unless a `title` key is passed; the four new icon-only buttons pass none, so they render as buttons with no accessible name. Sibling admin templates do pass title (backups_index.hbs:24,27), and no admin.embedding key exists for save/cancel/delete.

`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` splices the setting value straight into the statement with no quoting; a host containing an apostrophe terminates the literal and aborts the migration. The repo's own precedent escapes first — 20140929204155_migrate_tos_setting.rb:12 calls PG::Connection.escape_string before interpolating.

String.prototype.replace with a string pattern replaces only the first match, so it works for 'embeddable_host' (one underscore) and silently fails the ADMIN_MODELS lookup for any future two-underscore type; a /_/g regex is needed.

`attributes :id, :host, :category_id` already generates readers that delegate to read_attribute_for_serialization, so the three explicit `def x; object.x; end` methods (and EmbeddingSerializer's `id`) are exact duplicates of the generated behaviour.

Both `[0]['id']` on the categories join and `[0]['value']` on the uncategorized_category_id lookup index a PG::Result without checking cmd_tuples; PG::Result#[] raises IndexError when empty. The uncategorized_category_id row is only inserted by db/fixtures/001_categories.rb, which runs after migrations, so it can be absent too.

The test calls store.find('fruit', 2) but asserts colors [1,2], which are apple's (id 1) color_ids; banana (id 2) has [3]. The pretender handler for '/fruits/:id' ignores request.params and always returns fruits[0], so the test can neither fail on a wrong id nor verify per-record hydration.

The final statement deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category rows it just read, inside a `def change` whose `execute` calls are irreversible. If the unescaped/unnormalized insert produced wrong rows, the original configuration is unrecoverable.
Same unparameterized `VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)` interpolation; the value originates from an admin-editable site setting, so it is attacker-influenced input reaching raw SQL.
Confirmed by running the regex: `[a-z]{2,5}` rejects 'example.museum' and 'example.software'. Same defect as c003.

Interpolation is unescaped as described, and `val.split("\n")` keeps interior empty strings, so a setting value with a blank line inserts a row with host = '' into a column declared NOT NULL but not checked for blankness.

`force: true` is the established pattern in this repo (16 of 110 migrations use it, e.g. 20150325190959_create_queued_posts.rb, 20150318143915_create_directory_items.rb), and Rails never re-runs a recorded migration, so the 'data loss on re-run' consequence cannot occur for a table this migration itself introduces.

Grepping app/assets/javascripts for 'admin.embedding' finds confirm_delete, title, host, category and add_host in use; `edit` is referenced nowhere — the edit button is icon-only with no label or title.

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id; update then reaches `host.host = ...` and destroy calls `host.destroy`, both NoMethodError on nil, giving a 500 instead of a 404.

The controller implements only create/update/destroy, but a bare `resources` declares all seven routes. The repo does restrict elsewhere (config/routes.rb:122-129 uses `only:` for staff_action_logs, screened_emails, screened_urls).

Verified in ruby: "example.com\n" matches the regex because \Z permits a trailing newline, where \z would not. A stored host with a trailing newline would then never match record_for_host's exact comparison.
Same finding as c016/c022 — the embeddable_hosts site setting value is interpolated into the INSERT with no quoting or escaping.

The embedded factual part is true — the diff adds no acceptance test and the two new controller specs only check inheritance — but 'does the screen work end-to-end' is a runtime question. Settling it needs the app booted with gems and node_modules, or an added acceptance test that drives /admin/customize/embedding.

`let(:host) { "eviltrout.com" }` survives, but every `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = host` that referenced it was replaced by Fabricate(:embeddable_host) in this diff; nothing in the file reads `host` any more.

site_settings only holds rows for settings changed from their default, and embed_category defaults to '' (config/site_settings.yml, removed in this diff). The INNER JOIN therefore returns zero rows on any site that never customized it — and on fresh installs where categories is empty — and [0]['id'] raises IndexError, aborting rake db:migrate.

store.find branches on `typeof findArgs === "object"`; with findArgs undefined that is false, so it takes the else branch and returns _hydrate(type, result['embedding'], result) — a single record, not a ResultSet. The custom adapter (admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6) supplies the fixed path, so no id is needed.

The mechanism is stated loosely — PollFeed does reach EmbeddableHost matching, via TopicEmbed.import — but the consequence holds: the category now comes solely from a matching EmbeddableHost row for the feed item's URL, and feed-polling sites that never registered the feed host lose the embed_category setting with no replacement, so imported topics land in uncategorized.
Same defect as c020: the '/fruits/:id' pretender returns fruits[0] regardless of the requested id, so find('fruit', 2) is asserted against apple's data.

The migration adds no index at all and the model declares only validates_format_of, so nothing prevents two rows with the same host. record_for_host's `.first` then picks an arbitrary row, making which category applies nondeterministic.
Same observation as c006 — the only example is the `< Admin::AdminController` assertion; no CRUD action is invoked.

`obj[k].map(...)` is reached for any key matching /(.+)_ids$/ with no type check, so a JSON null (or a scalar) for that key throws a TypeError inside hydration. The singular branch has no equivalent exposure because it just passes the value along.

The before_validation block calls `self.host.sub!` unguarded; I confirmed nil.sub! raises NoMethodError. save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] straight through, so a create/update posted without a host 500s inside validation instead of returning a validation error.
Same finding as c007 — the two files' contents are exchanged.

The raw INSERT bypasses the model, so values the old host_list setting accepted with a scheme or path ('https://example.com/1234' — the very shape the new specs fabricate) are stored verbatim. record_for_host compares them to URI(...).host, a bare hostname, so migrated rows stop matching and embedding silently breaks after upgrade.

Both halves check out: before_validation strips `/.*$` before validates_format_of runs, so the regex's `(\/.*)?` branch is unreachable, and the `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` branch permits a port that URI(...).host never produces, so such a row can never match.

Verified by running the regex: 'localhost' does not match, because a literal dot plus a 2-5 letter TLD is mandatory. Embedding on a local dev host cannot be registered (embed_controller.rb:60 has a dev-admin bypass, but only for admins in Rails.env.development?).

The redundancy is real — Admin::AdminController already declares both filters and neither subclass needs to repeat them. The stated consequence is wrong though: ActiveSupport::Callbacks de-duplicates symbol filters (CallbackChain#append_one removes duplicates before pushing), so they run once, not twice.

`hydrated` is the return value of Array#map, which is always an array, so the `|| []` alternative can never be taken. It reads as a guard against a failure mode that does not exist, while the failure that does exist (undefined elements inside the array) is unhandled.
Same defect as c017; the worked example is correct — 'my_embedded_host'.replace('_','-') yields 'my-embedded_host', which is not in ADMIN_MODELS, so basePath would return '/' instead of '/admin/'.

save_host rewrites a blank category_id to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, but the callback sets `category` from the component's own categoryId — Discourse.Category.findById(null) is undefined — instead of from the serialized response, so the row renders with an empty category badge while the server has persisted uncategorized.

The asymmetry the question points at is real and checkable: the migration joins `s.value = c.name`, i.e. it only handles a category name, while the code that consumed the setting (TopicCreator#find_category) accepted an integer or numeric string id as well. Sites that stored an id therefore get no match and fall back to uncategorized, losing their configuration.

Grepping the templates shows no {{action "saveChanges"}} anywhere under admin/templates for this screen — embedding.hbs only wires addHost — so the saveChanges action, the PUT route and EmbeddingController#update are never exercised; saving happens per row through embeddable-host.js.es6.
update's body is identical to show's: it re-serializes the OpenStruct built by fetch_embedding and never reads params or writes anything, so a PUT reports success while persisting nothing.
Same defect as c017/c047 — string-pattern replace touches only the first underscore.
Same defect as c039 — the branch is entered on the key name alone and calls .map without an Array.isArray check, so a null or scalar value throws.
